title: Diabetes, hypertension and CKD together
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, kidney disease and any related hypertension and dialysis status.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for management of chronic conditions.

HPI
The patient is an 81-year-old male presenting for a scheduled follow-up of his chronic medical conditions. He reports feeling generally well today but notes persistent fatigue. He is currently managing his type 2 diabetes through dietary modifications alone and reports no recent episodes of significant illness. He continues to manage his hypertension and chronic kidney disease. He denies any acute shortness of breath or recent changes in his mobility.

Medication List
Lisinopril 10mg daily
Amlodipine 5mg daily

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented x3. He appears in no acute distress. Vital signs are stable with a blood pressure of 132/78 mmHg. Heart sounds are regular with no murmurs. Lungs are clear to auscultation. No peripheral edema noted in lower extremities.

Assessment
1. End stage renal disease: Recent labs show an eGFR of 12 mL/min/1.73m2.
2. Hypertension: Currently stable on oral medications.
3. Type 2 diabetes: Managed with diet.
4. Chronic kidney disease.

Plan
Continue current antihypertensive regimen. Maintain current diet for management of type 2 diabetes. Monitor renal function with repeat labs in three months.

Electronically signed, J. Lindqvist, PA-C, 05/14/2026
explanations: Type 2 diabetes and CKD are linked by the 'with' convention unless the provider says otherwise: E11.22 (HCC 37).
Hypertension with CKD stage 5 or ESRD: I12.0 (HCC 326).
The CKD stage is coded in addition: N18.6.

distractors.why: The 'with' convention presumes the diabetes caused the CKD.
I12.9 is for stage 1-4 or unspecified CKD.
Hypertension and CKD are presumed linked: I12.-, not I10.
E11.22 says to use an additional code for the CKD stage.
